name: Pan-Zoom Canvas
summary: The viewport model from design tools: wheel and pinch zoom toward the cursor, space-drag pans, the dot grid moves with the world, and a minimap shows where you are.

attempts.problem: Zoomed around the origin, so the content slid away from the cursor as it scaled and reaching a specific node meant zooming then panning to find it again. The background grid stayed fixed while the content moved, which made panning read as the content sliding over a sheet rather than the viewport moving across one — the single clearest signal that a canvas is fake.

attempts.prompt: Zoom toward the cursor and make the grid move with the content.
attempts.problem: Zoom-to-cursor worked with a wheel but pinch on a trackpad still zoomed around the origin, because trackpad pinch arrives as a wheel event with ctrlKey set and was falling through to the pan branch. Keyboard users had no way to move at all, and left-drag panned unconditionally, so selecting or clicking anything inside the canvas was impossible.

finalPrompt:
Build a pan and zoom canvas in plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript, no dependencies.

Zoom must keep the point under the cursor fixed. Convert the cursor position into world coordinates, apply the new scale, then translate so that same world point lands back under the cursor. Zooming around the origin makes the content flee the pointer and is the difference between a canvas that feels like a tool and one that feels broken.

Trackpad pinch arrives as a wheel event with ctrlKey set, not as a gesture event. Detect it and use a larger factor, or pinch will feel dead compared with the scroll wheel.

The background grid belongs to the world. Scale its background-size by the zoom and offset its background-position by the translation, so panning reads as the viewport moving across a surface rather than content sliding over a fixed sheet.

Do not pan on plain left-drag. Pan on middle-drag, or left-drag while space is held, so clicking things inside the canvas remains possible. Call setPointerCapture so a fast pan that leaves the element keeps tracking.

Give it a full keyboard path: arrows pan, Shift pans faster, plus and minus zoom about the centre, zero fits the content. Put role="application" and a label on the container stating those keys, since this is a genuine application widget rather than a document.

Show the current zoom as a percentage and a minimap whose rectangle reflects the visible fraction of the world and its position, clamped so it never leaves the minimap.

Clamp scale between about 0.35 and 3.5, and recompute the fit on resize.

Colour comes only from CSS custom properties: var(--bg), var(--surface), var(--raised), var(--border), var(--text), var(--text-dim), var(--accent), var(--mono). No literal hex, rgb or hsl values.
why:
Zoom-to-cursor is four lines of arithmetic and it is the entire difference between this feeling like Figma and feeling like a broken slideshow. It is also never volunteered, because zooming about the origin is simpler and looks fine in a screenshot. Describing the mechanism step by step — to world space, scale, translate back — produced it correctly first time, where asking for zoom to cursor had produced an approximation.

The pinch detail is the kind of platform fact that cannot be reasoned out. Trackpad pinch is a ctrl-wheel event, and a component that does not know that feels dead to half its users on hardware the developer may not be testing on. Facts like this belong in the prompt as facts.

The pan-modifier decision is a design choice with an accessibility consequence: panning on plain left-drag makes everything inside the canvas unclickable. Stating the requirement as clicking things inside the canvas must remain possible gets the right binding without prescribing it.
